question: Should `2026.7.1-2` become the default gateway package after the upstream startup report is dispositioned and the supported Windows/WSL acceptance matrix succeeds?
rationale: A last-known-good promotion is a release-readiness decision: source review can confirm the pin location, but it cannot establish that the selected external gateway package is safe for the supported installation and recovery paths.

options.title: Validate then promote
options.body: Collect the exact-version Windows/WSL setup, health, pairing, repair, and rollback evidence, record the upstream-report disposition, then merge the centralized pin.

options.title: Keep the existing LKG
options.body: Leave `2026.6.11` as the default until the candidate's startup risk and supported-path acceptance are resolved.

options.title: Accept the release risk
options.body: Approve the new default without the requested acceptance matrix, explicitly accepting the possibility of setup and repair failures.

recommendation.title: Validate then promote
recommendation.body: Collect the exact-version Windows/WSL setup, health, pairing, repair, and rollback evidence, record the upstream-report disposition, then merge the centralized pin.

likelyOwner.reason: Their review identifies the exact release-readiness evidence and unresolved upstream risk that need a release-owner disposition.
